records.public_claim_text: The impact of climate change, including extreme weather events and rising temperatures, changing patterns of work, fast technological advances, and the global COVID-19 pandemic have all introduced new pressing concerns for safety and health at work.

records.public_claim_text: Workers are exposed to dangerous machinery, strenuous physical tasks and poor work ergonomics, putting them at risk of fatalities, injuries, illnesses, and long-term health implications.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Workers are exposed to dangerous machinery, strenuous physical tasks and poor work ergonomics, putting them at risk of fatalities, injuries, illnesses, and long-term health implications.

records.public_claim_text: The latest estimates developed by the ILO cover the year 2019 and are used for the first time in this report.1 According to these latest estimates, over 395 million workers worldwide sustained a non-fatal work injury in 2019.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: The latest estimates developed by the ILO cover the year 2019 and are used for the first time in this report.1 According to these latest estimates, over 395 million workers worldwide sustained a non-fatal work injury in 2019.

records.public_claim_text: These estimates are based on the latest estimation method by Jukka Takala and colleagues (see Hämäläinen, 2017), which was further updated specifically for this purpose.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: These estimates are based on the latest estimation method by Jukka Takala and colleagues (see Hämäläinen, 2017), which was further updated specifically for this purpose.

records.public_claim_text: The attributable fraction of work-related deaths is estimated to be highest in Africa (7.39 per cent), followed by Asia and the Pacific (7.13 per cent) and Oceania (6.52 per cent).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: The attributable fraction of work-related deaths is estimated to be highest in Africa (7.39 per cent), followed by Asia and the Pacific (7.13 per cent) and Oceania (6.52 per cent).

records.public_claim_text: Work-related deaths are unequally distributed, with the male mortality rate (51.4 per 100,000 working age adults) much higher than the female rate (17.2 per 100,000).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Work-related deaths are unequally distributed, with the male mortality rate (51.4 per 100,000 working age adults) much higher than the female rate (17.2 per 100,000).

records.public_claim_text: To date, 42 pairs of occupational risk factors and associated health outcomes (namely a specific disease or injury) have been studied (ILO & WHO 2021a, Pega et al., 2023).

records.public_claim_text: According to these estimates, a total of 90.22 million disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) were attributable to these 42 specific pairs.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: According to these estimates, a total of 90.22 million disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) were attributable to these 42 specific pairs.

records.public_claim_text: The ILO estimated that in 2019 the mining industry contributed to about 3 per cent of fatal accidents at work and the estimated fatality rate was found to be four times higher than the global average of all sectors (ILO forthcoming).

records.public_claim_text: Recent events such as the explosion of a large store of ammonium nitrate in the Beirut port (Lebanon) in 2020 and an explosion in a waste management centre in Leverkusen (Germany) in 2021, serve as stark reminders of the devastating consequences that can occur when adequate measures to prevent and control risks are not properly implemented.
